summary.whatChanges: Adds a new public `toZod<T>()` helper to Zod v4 core, classic, and mini. It returns the schema unchanged at runtime but type-checks at compile time that the schema's output type exactly equals `T`, emitting per-key mismatch diagnostics for object schemas. Documentation and type-level tests are added.
behaviorChanges: `z.toZod<T>()(schema)` is now exported from zod/v4 classic, zod/mini, zod/v4/core, and core `util`
Schemas whose output type is not exactly `T` (extra keys, missing optional keys, wrong property types, missing `readonly`, bare `z.any()`) now fail to compile
Object schema mismatches report the specific offending key with `expected`/`received` in the type error
The returned value keeps the original schema type, so members like `.shape.username` and chained methods remain available
Docs gain a "Matching an existing type" section contrasting `toZod` with `satisfies z.ZodType<T>`
risks: The recursive mapped/conditional types (`ToZodShape`, `ToZodTarget`) could trigger excessive type instantiation depth or slow type-checking on large schemas
Exact equality is asymmetric: intersection targets only match `.and()` and flat targets only match `.safeExtend()`, which is likely to surprise users
Runtime implementation is a bare `as any` identity cast, so no validation is performed and the guarantee is purely compile-time
Adding a new `toZod` export to classic/mini/core barrels could collide with existing user re-exports or wildcard imports
